title: Display & monitors
blurb: Second monitor, docks, blurry or tiny text, flicker, projectors.

remedies.title: Mouse goes off the wrong edge between two monitors
remedies.why: The system thinks the screens are placed differently from your desk.

steps.text: Settings › Display › Identify, then drag the boxes to match your desk and Apply. Set the main display there too.
Displays › Arrange…: drag the screens to match; drag the menu bar to the main one.

remedies.title: Screen is upside down or sideways
remedies.why: Display orientation was changed (often by a shortcut or a rotating monitor).

steps.text: Settings › Display › Display orientation › Landscape. (Some PCs: Ctrl+Alt+Up arrow.)
Displays › the screen › Rotation › Standard.

remedies.title: Colours look wrong, washed out or inverted
remedies.why: A colour filter, HDR, or a cable/monitor colour setting is on.

steps.text: Turn off Color filters (Accessibility › Color filters; shortcut Windows+Ctrl+C).
Turn HDR off if a monitor looks washed out: Settings › Display › Use HDR.
Turn off Invert colours and Colour filters in Accessibility › Display.
Calibrate colours.
Reset the monitor's own picture settings with its buttons.

remedies.title: Use a laptop closed with an external monitor
remedies.why: By default closing the lid sleeps the laptop.

steps.text: Power options › Choose what closing the lid does › Plugged in: Do nothing.
Mac clamshell mode works when it's charging and has an external keyboard/mouse and display connected.

remedies.title: My 120/144 Hz monitor only runs at 60 Hz
remedies.why: The cable, port or adapter doesn't carry high refresh rates, or the setting wasn't changed.

steps.text: Settings › Display › Advanced display › Choose a refresh rate.
Displays › the monitor › Refresh rate.
Use DisplayPort or a good HDMI 2.0+/USB-C cable; cheap adapters cap at 60 Hz.

remedies.title: Screen turns off or locks too quickly
remedies.why: Power saving turns the screen off; your workplace may set a lock time.

steps.text: Settings › System › Power & battery › Screen and sleep.
Lock Screen › Turn display off when inactive.

remedies.escalate: Work devices often have a required lock time; IT sets it.

remedies.title: USB monitor or dock shows nothing on a Mac (DisplayLink)
remedies.why: DisplayLink docks need the DisplayLink Manager app running and permission to capture the screen.

steps.text: Install DisplayLink Manager from Synaptics' site and open it.
Allow it in Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording.
Set it to start at login.

remedies.title: Lines, spots or dead pixels on the screen
remedies.why: If they show on screenshots too it's software; if not, it's the panel or its cable.

steps.text: Take a screenshot: lines in the screenshot = graphics/driver; lines only on the screen = hardware.
Connect an external monitor; if it's fine, the laptop panel or its cable is at fault.
Update the graphics driver for the software case.

remedies.escalate: Hardware lines need a repair; tell IT the model and whether it changes when you move the lid.
